title: Samsung taps Mistral AI models for semiconductor manufacturing
slides: Samsung bets on Mistral AI—can it fix chip yields?
Mistral's models now assist Samsung's semiconductor production.
The twist: these AI models run on EUV tools, not clouds.
Engineers get real-time defect analysis without human review.
Your next chip may hide which model actually printed it.
thread_text:
1. Who's really printing your chip?

Samsung just put Mistral's AI on EUV scanners — the machines that etch your phone's brain.

2. Defect review without a human

The AI spots flaws in real time on EUV tools, a task that once took engineers hours.

3. The twist: on the tool, not the cloud

Mistral's models run locally inside the scanner — data never leaves the fab.

4. The yield gamble

Samsung's chip yields have lagged rivals. This AI could be the fix — or a risky bet.

5. Ask your next phone

Ask your next phone chip's maker: was it designed or printed by an AI? Does it matter?

instagram.caption:
The machine that prints your phone’s brain now watches its own mistakes—no human needed.  

Samsung just plugged Mistral’s AI directly into its EUV scanners, the tools that etch chips. The AI spots defects in real time, on the machine itself, not in some distant cloud. Engineers skip hours of manual review.  

This is a bet on fixing Samsung’s lagging chip yields—fewer wasted wafers, cheaper production. For you, that could mean faster, cheaper silicon in your next device.  

But if the AI screws up, who audits the auditor?  

Would you trust a chip that was printed by an AI you never see? 🔍⚙️💾
